# `layout/auth`

Sign-in, registration and recovery pages share a centred card and optional split panel.

## Selection

- **Use when:** Sign-in, registration and recovery pages share a centred card and optional split panel.
- **Avoid when:** The page sits inside the authenticated shell.
- **Consider instead:** `layout/page`, `layout/containers`
- **Stability:** stable.

## Import

```tsx fragment — import-only example
import { AuthCard } from "themelia-ui/layout/auth"
import "themelia-ui/layout/auth.css"
```

## Composition

This family composes `base/cards`, `base/typography`.

Application policy—routing, fetching, persistence, permissions, and translation—stays
outside the package and arrives through the public props, callbacks, slots, or accessors below.

| `strings` | no | `Partial<AuthShellStrings>` | Overrides this shell's own copy — the three link rows' names. |

### `AuthSplitPanel`

Kind: callable.

Form beside a panel, for a caller composing both halves itself. `AuthShell
variant="split"` is the same arrangement with the shell's own card.

## Preview recipes

Preview route: Auth shells — `/auth-shell`

### Card · a complete sign-in page

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<AuthShell
  brand={brand}
  title="Welcome back"
  description="Sign in to your Acme workspace."
  cardFooter={<Text size="xs">Local demo · no account required</Text>}
  policyLinks={policy}
>
  <YourSignInForm />
</AuthShell>
```

### Bare · a quiet canvas

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<AuthShell variant="bare" size="sm" brand={brand}
  title="Make yourself at home" policyLinks={policy}>
  <YourSignInForm />
</AuthShell>
```

### Split · a story beside the form

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<AuthShell variant="split" splitSide="start" splitMobile="stacked"
  splitPanel={<WorkspaceStory />} brand={brand} title="Good to see you again">
  <YourSignInForm />
</AuthShell>
```

### Composed · bring your own surface

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<AuthSplitPanel
  panelMobile="stacked"
  form={<Stack gap="xl">
    <AuthCard title="Join your team" headerEnd={<Badge>Invite</Badge>}>
      <YourSignInForm />
    </AuthCard>
    <AuthFooterLinks label="Legal" links={policy} />
  </Stack>}
  panel={<WorkspaceInvitation />}
/>
```
